newsitem.title: JAPAN: Timing of Japan election up to prime minister - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Timing of Japan election up to prime minister - MOF.

text.p: The timing of general elections in Japan is up to the political judgement of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, but Japan must for now put priority on the redevelopment of Okinawa prefecture, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Friday.

Asked about the possibility of snap elections in October, reported by Japanese media today, Kubo said: "The decision to dissolve parliament is up to the prime minister's political judgement, but I think what is most important now is to seek a good solution to Okinawa's current issues."

The small southern island prefecture of Okinawa houses 75 percent of all the U.S. military facilities based in Japan. On Sunday, Okinawa will hold a non-binding referendum on whether the bases should be phased out.

Last month, the 15-member Grand Bench of the Supreme Court ruled unanimously that Okinawa must appropriate land for U.S. military bases, rejecting an appeal by Okinawa's governor that the military presence was unconstitutional.

Concerning a supplementary budget for the current 1996/97 fiscal year, Kubo said the government will naturally draft a supplementary budget this year to finance the necessary additional costs for the government, but this does not mean a large-scale extra budget aimed at stimulating the economy.
